summary: Shows the `or` form of failed_when, splitting long conditions across lines with YAML `>`, and using the implicit `_task` variable (`_task.result`) to check results without `register`. `_task` works in `when`, `until`, `failed_when`, `changed_when`, and `break_when`.
questions: How do I write a long failed_when with many OR conditions?
Can I check a task's result in failed_when without registering it?

answer_card.title: Multi-line failed_when and the _task variable
answer_card.answer_md:
Split long OR conditions with `>`:
```yaml
- ansible.builtin.shell: "./myBinary"
  register: ret
  failed_when: >
    ("No such file or directory" in ret.stdout) or
    (ret.stderr != '') or
    (ret.rc == 10)
```

Or skip `register` and use the implicit `_task` variable:
```yaml
- ansible.builtin.command: /usr/bin/example-command
  failed_when: _task.result.rc != 0 or 'ERROR' in _task.result.stdout
```
`_task` works in all conditional keywords: `when`, `until`, `failed_when`, `changed_when`, and `break_when`.
